The Admin Console description states that staff reach the console with the same SSO accounts and sign‑in path as customers and that an `is_admin` flag enables console functions, which supports the noted limitation that administrator access uses the same SSO path as customers and is not via a stronger access path. quoted_text.text:
### Identity Service

Authenticates customers, drivers, and staff. All interactive sign-in is delegated to the
company's SSO provider over OpenID Connect; the service issues short-lived internal tokens
that the core services verify.

### Admin Console

The staff interface for refunds, address corrections, and account management. Staff reach
the console with the same SSO accounts and the same sign-in path customers use; an
`is_admin` flag on the user record enables the console's functions. The console can read
and edit any customer account, order, and address.

assessments.rationale: The Admin Console description directly supports that it is the staff interface for refunds, address corrections, and account management, that staff reach it using the same SSO accounts and sign-in path as customers, that an `is_admin` flag on the user record enables the console's functions, and that the console can read and edit any customer account, order, and address. This backs the existence of an `is_admin` flag gating console functions and the global read/write capability. However, the stronger claim that these functions are enabled *only* for users whose record carries `is_admin` is an inference from "enables the console's functions" rather than an explicit exclusivity statement, and the limitation that administrators have global access "without finer-grained roles or scoping" goes beyond what is written (the documentation is silent on whether any additional role model exists). The staff-operator actor entry is consistent with this but does not add detail on authorization granularity. Therefore the control and its first limitation are supported, but the stronger exclusivity and "no finer-grained roles" aspects are not fully established by the text.
missing_evidence: Documentation of the full authorization and role model for the Admin Console, including whether any roles or scopes beyond a single `is_admin` flag exist and whether non-`is_admin` accounts can access any console functionality.

# Parcelworks — Platform Overview

Parcelworks is a parcel-logistics platform: customers book and track shipments, drivers
collect and deliver them, and carrier partners handle line-haul between depots. This
document describes the platform as deployed across its four zones: edge, core, data, and
operations.

### Notification Service

Sends booking confirmations, delivery windows, and delivery notices by email and SMS
through an external messaging provider. For debugging, the notification templates log the
full rendered message body — including the recipient's name, delivery address, and delivery
window — to the shared application log.

assessments.rationale: The platform overview lists the main zones and components of Parcelworks but does not mention any AI/ML or model-based component. This suggests that model output is not a first-class architectural element, but absence of mention is not sufficient to prove that no model-generated content is ever produced or published. The reasoning that req-AI-002 is not applicable to thr-001 because no model output is published therefore rests on an assumption rather than on explicit documentation of model non-use or of the threat path.
missing_evidence: Documentation clearly stating whether the system uses any AI/ML models whose outputs are rendered or published to users.
Threat-model material for thr-001 indicating whether any model-generated content appears on the attack path.
